text:
Maya: FYI customer reporting a weird issue — their request IDs sometimes don't map to full traces in the console, spans are missing intermittently. customer sent request-id: 0x7a9b3c (Acme). Screenshot shows only ingress span.
Olivia (Acme): yes — we see the API returning 200, but the trace view only has the initial span and then nothing. happened for ~10% of requests this morning. happening across regions.
Maya: tagging @eng-runtime and @sre. Can you advise quick triage steps? Customer is getting nervous about data completeness.
Dan: thanks. can you share a sample request-id and approximate timestamps? Also: are they using our sdk or raw requests?
Maya: sample request-id 0x7a9b3c, seen at 2026-03-15T09:12:34Z. They're using raw HTTP (curl from their infra). Attached their simplified request headers:
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Request-ID: 0x7a9b3c
Content-Type: application/json
```
Maya: they also forwarded our ingest logs showing a 200 on /generate and an entry in trace-ingest: `ingest_id=2324 req_id=0x7a9b3c status=accepted` but downstream trace link shows `no parent found` in the trace indexer logs.
Jamie: quick check — does the request-id get rewritten / truncated in any gateway? If the header exceeds expected length it might be dropped during propagation. Also possible mismatch between request-id header and internal trace id mapping.
Dan: pulling the indexer logs for that window... hold.
tracebot: [automated] deploys to trace-indexer prod rolling update at 2026-03-15T08:40:00Z by jamie — version v1.12.3.
Dan: saw something: indexer logs show two entries for ingest_id=2324. First with req_id=0x7a9b3c then later `req_id=0x7a9b3c...` (truncated) in the span-link worker. Looks like a truncation/encoding issue where very long header values get a suffix added by our ELB (`...`) during rotation. That means the request-id in the span store doesn't exactly match the mapping key used by trace-linker.
Maya: customer said some of their request IDs are UUIDs concatenated with extra metadata — long strings. Could be hitting a length boundary.
Jamie: repro plan: 1) send requests with X-Request-ID lengths: 36 (uuid), 120, 200 chars. 2) observe trace-ingest and span-linker entries. 3) check if mapping fails when header > 128 chars. I'll run a small script from my laptop.
Jamie: (after test) confirmed: when header length > 128, our edge/ELB injects an internal marker which we then sanitize improperly, resulting in a mismatch. span-linker uses the raw header as key; trace-indexer normalizes it differently — bug.
Dan: ok root cause identified: inconsistent normalization of request-id between ingest and linker when header length exceeds 128. That explains intermittent nature (depends on client request-id format).
Maya: customer impact: some percentage of spans appear as 'ghost' (only ingress) because link lookup fails.
Jamie: proposed fix: ensure a single normalization function in the ingestion path and canonicalize to first 128 chars with a checksum suffix to avoid collisions. I'll open a PR and deploy canary to trace-linker and indexer.
Jamie: PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/9876 — adds normalize_request_id() and tests.
Dan: plan for rollout: canary to 10% traffic in us-east for 30m, monitor missing-span rate and error budget, then 100% if green. I'll handle canary.
Maya: I've informed the customer and asked for a short verification window after canary. They can toggle some of their long-id traffic.
Olivia (Acme): thanks — we'd appreciate a heads-up before the canary. We can send some test traffic.
Dan: starting canary now. metrics: missing_span_rate baseline for Acme was 8.1% across last hour.
tracebot: [automated] canary rollout started: trace-linker v1.12.4-canary (10% traffic) at 2026-03-15T09:45:00Z.
Jamie: logs look good on canary, normalization applied. sample match for long request-id now succeeds: `req_id_normalized=0x7a9b3c|chk=4f2a` linking span_id=...
Dan: monitoring: missing_span_rate for Acme dropped from 8.1% to 0.6% within 12 minutes. no increase in latency (p95 token latency unchanged).
Olivia (Acme): verified on our side — traces look complete for the long-id samples we just sent. thank you :tada:
Maya: good to hear. Jamie, can you cut a patch release and schedule a full rollout? Also add a migration note to changelog and a quick KB for customers about request-id length limits.
Jamie: will do. patch release v1.12.4 merging now, full rollout in 2h if canary stays green.
Dan: marking this escalated -> resolved pending post-rollout monitoring. I'll keep the customer looped in.
Maya: thanks team. closing the loop with Acme once full rollout is done.
Olivia (Acme): thanks everyone for the fast turnaround. we appreciate the clear repro steps and fix.
